claims.claim: The page animates and it honours `prefers-reduced-motion` — motion here is decoration, and the page must stay complete when it is off. (Animated GIFs are outside its reach: a GIF cannot honour reduced-motion, and the three in the README are a deliberate exception.)
claims.value: animated and reducible
claims.metric: pages containing `animation:`/`@keyframes` vs pages containing `prefers-reduced-motion`
claims.method: the check walks every committed .html page and covers all three ways a page moves — CSS animations/keyframes, SVG SMIL, and requestAnimationFrame — requiring a `prefers-reduced-motion` reference wherever it finds one. It does not judge what the fallback does, only that a branch exists, because a missing branch is invisible in review and obvious to the person it affects. It does not cover animated GIFs, which no CSS can switch off — the README embeds three of them, and that medium's fallback is the reader's own browser settings, not a branch in this repository.

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re

# 三种动效来源：CSS 动画/关键帧、SVG SMIL、以及 JS 的 requestAnimationFrame。
MOVES = re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|<animate\b|<animateTransform\b|requestAnimationFrame')
RELAX = 'prefers-reduced-motion'
pages = sorted(p for p in list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('*.html'))
               + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('docs/*.html')) if p.name != 'template.html')
animated, missing = 0, []
for p in pages:
    t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if MOVES.search(t):
        animated += 1
        if RELAX not in t:
            missing.append(p.name)
print('pages', len(pages), 'animated', animated, 'missing', missing)
assert animated and not missing
PY

source.quote: The prefers-reduced-motion CSS media feature is used to detect if a user has enabled a setting on their device to minimize the amount of non-essential motion.
